_about: Per-paper provenance for the flat peptide datasets in this directory. One entry per <key>.tsv. Every 'conditions_quote' and 'conversion_quote' is VERBATIM from the source text; anything derived is marked as derived.

_audit_cycle_87.what: Independent adversarial re-verification of all nine TSVs against the printed tables, requested by the question's owner. Ground truth was re-transcribed by eye from pages rendered at 200-450 dpi, NOT by re-running the extractors, and compared cell by cell. Route per dataset: reasoning/evidence/scripts/verify_peptide_tsvs.py.
_audit_cycle_87.result: 197 peptides, 9 datasets, 0 transcription errors. Every sequence, cap assignment, n_res, pH, temperature and ionic strength in the shipped TSVs reproduces its source. Cells compared: Viguera 44, Padmanabhan 16, Chakrabartty 1993 14, Doig Table 1 50, Doig Table 3 50, Huygues Asp 56, Huygues AspArg 32, Chakrabartty 1994 58 peptides x 7 fields, Petukhov 30 peptides x 8 fields.
independent_corroborations_that_held: Chakrabartty 1994's 11 'c'-flagged rows reproduce Doig Table 1's pH-9.55 column exactly, and both transcriptions were made independently of each other.
Doig Tables 1 and 3: 94 of 95 populated cells satisfy footnote b's theta/34,100 to within 0.002; the exceptions are the paper's own rounding.
Petukhov: Chen 1974 with n = 15 peptide bonds reproduces every printed %helix to a mean 0.24 points - so the two stored columns are mutually consistent.
Padmanabhan: all four orderings the paper asserts in prose (6X10L > 6X9L, 9L13X > 10L13X, and X C-terminal to Leu > X N-terminal, for all four residues) hold in the data.
Chakrabartty 1993: the three rows whose single value a naive parse would put in column a (aak, fak, aa-ak20) are in column b in the shipped data, as the render shows.
_audit_cycle_87.what_was_wrong_instead: All defects found were in PROSE, not data: this manifest's theta_H-convention claim (five conventions, actually two), its 'buffers as in Table 1' claim for Doig Table 3, its identical-row-pair list for that table, its attribution of Viguera's NMR concentration to the CD measurements, a silently corrected 'verbatim' quote under Petukhov, a stale not_yet_extracted pointer, and the omission of the buffer's own contribution from every coded ionic strength. Plus one real data defect OUTSIDE these files, in munoz_1997_figure_4_data.json figure4A. Each is recorded in place.
_audit_cycle_87.ionic_strength_systematic: The coded ionic strengths are salt concentrations with the buffer's contribution omitted. Immaterial wherever 1 M NaCl dominates (<=5%). Material at the low-salt end, which is exactly where these datasets were wanted: Petukhov 1.8x (pH 7) and 3.0x (pH 10) low, Huygues low-salt rows 1.7x low at pH 7 but only 1.07x at pH 2.25 - so a pH comparison carries a 1.6x ionic-strength difference coded as zero. Computed in reasoning/evidence/scripts/ionic_strength.py, table in reasoning/evidence/data/ionic_strength.txt. NOT applied to the coded values, because they feed the scored suite and that is the owner's call.
_audit_cycle_87.followup_cycle_92: The cycle-87 audit compared this dataset's TSV against the PDF's text layer and reported 0 problems. That was true and it was not enough: the text layer faithfully reproduces a typo in the printed table (V4, above). The cycle-92 pre-submission audit of REFERENCE_RUN_LIST.tsv caught it, because a duplicated sequence collapses two runs into one and that is visible downstream where it is invisible in the file itself. LESSON, worth keeping: 'the file matches its source' is a weaker check than 'the file satisfies the invariants its source implies'. The other eight datasets were verified against RENDERED PAGES rather than text layers and a cross-dataset duplicate sweep now covers all nine - the only remaining shared sequences are the eight Doig side-chain ionisation pairs, which are expected.

1998_petukhov_jmb278.citation: Petukhov, M., Munoz, V., Yumoto, N., Yoshikawa, S. & Serrano, L. (1998). Position dependence of non-polar amino acid intrinsic helical propensities. J. Mol. Biol. 278, 279-289.
1998_petukhov_jmb278.source_text: doc/1998_petukhov_Position dependence of non-polar amino acid intrinsic helical propensities.txt
1998_petukhov_jmb278.source_table: Table 1 - 'Sequences and results of CD measurements of the helical contents for the series of synthetic peptides used in this study'
1998_petukhov_jmb278.conditions_quote: Table 1 footnote, as PRINTED: 'Far-UV CD spectra of the peptides were obtained at pH 10 (FX1 series), or pH 7 for the rest of the peptides, in 5 mM sodium phosphate buffer at 5C. Peptide concentrations were 50 mM.' / Methods: 'Circular dichroism (CD) spectra were recorded on a Jasco-710 instrument at pH 7 and a temperature of 278 K.'
1998_petukhov_jmb278.ionic_strength_derivation: DERIVED, not stated as an ionic strength, and coded LOW ON PURPOSE. 0.005 is the stated buffer CONCENTRATION. Computed at cycle 87 from the speciation (reasoning/evidence/scripts/ionic_strength.py): 5 mM sodium phosphate gives I = 0.0089 M at pH 7 (pKa2 = 7.20, an H2PO4-/HPO4(2-) mixture) and I = 0.0151 M at pH 10 (effectively all HPO4(2-)), before any NaOH used to reach pH 10. So the coded value is 1.8x low for the pH 7 rows and 3.0x low for the FX1 rows, AND - the part that matters - the two sets are coded at the SAME ionic strength when they actually differ by 1.7x. Left as the traceable lower bound rather than changed unilaterally, because it feeds the scored suite; flagged as the first candidate if the screening lever is revisited.
1998_petukhov_jmb278.caps: Taken from the sequence notation in the table, not inferred: 'NH2-...' = free N-terminus (coded ncap empty), 'Ac-...' = acetyl (Ac), '...-NH2' = amide (Am). The FX1 series is the free-amine set and is the reason those five rows are at pH 10.
1998_petukhov_jmb278.conversion_quote: The percentage of alpha-helix was calculated with the empirical equation -100(theta222/(39,500(1-2.57/n))) by Chen et al. (1974); where n is the number of peptide bonds and theta222 is an experimentally observed ellipticity of peptide at 222 nm.
1998_petukhov_jmb278.conversion_note: Chen 1974's -39,500*(1-2.57/n). This is the SECOND of two theta_H conventions in the corpus, not the third - see the corrected note under the Doig entries: -34,100 and -33,750 are both Scholtz 1991's -40,000*(1-2.5/n) evaluated at n = 17 and n = 16, not independent conventions. Checked here: 100*theta/(39,500*(1-2.57/n)) with n = 15 peptide bonds reproduces every printed %helix in this table to a mean |deviation| of 0.24 points (max 1.88); n = 16 gives 0.45 and n = 14 gives 0.68, so the paper's 'n is the number of peptide bonds' means 15 for these 16-residue peptides. Both quantities are stored as separate rows so no conversion is baked in.

quantities.minus_theta222: -[theta]222 as printed, deg cm2 dmol-1, with the paper's error
quantities.helix_percent: % helix as printed, with the paper's error

1998_petukhov_jmb278.why_it_matters: Scans Gly, Val, Ile, Leu and Met through N1, N2, N3, N4 and a central position on one poly-Ala host. It is the experimental basis for the position-dependent intrinsic propensities in table_1_lacroix.tsv, and it covers five residues of the fourteen that appear in NO reference-binary run.
1998_petukhov_jmb278.conditions_quote_note: ADDED at cycle 87. The footnote as printed says '50 mM'; the earlier version of this field silently rendered it '50 microM' while claiming to be verbatim. 50 mM peptide is not a CD concentration and the Methods give 'different dilutions of the peptides (10 microM to 500 microM)', so the printed mM is a typo for microM - but the correction now sits in this note rather than inside a quotation. The concentration is not a stored column, so nothing downstream changes. Separately: the Methods say CD was recorded 'at pH 7', which reads as a conflict with the footnote's pH 10 for the FX1 series. It is not - the Discussion states 'Since the non-blocked peptides at the N terminus were analyzed at pH 10, we did not expect any charge interactions of the free N-terminal group', so the pH 10 assignment for the five free-amine peptides is confirmed three ways and the Methods sentence is the general case.
1998_petukhov_jmb278.printed_table_error: FOUND AND CORRECTED AT CYCLE 92, during the pre-submission audit of REFERENCE_RUN_LIST.tsv. Table 1 prints V4's sequence as 'Ac-AAVAAAAARAAARGGY-NH2' - Val at position 3, character for character identical to V3 on the line above. Read at 900 dpi, so this is the PAGE and not the text layer. V4 is nonetheless a real and distinct peptide, on three independent grounds: (1) every other series in the same table steps by one and the Gly block sits directly above the Val block as a control - G1 GAAAAAAAR, G2 AGAAAAAAR, G3 AAGAAAAAR, G4 AAAGAAAAR, G7 AAAAAAGAR, and likewise Ile, Leu, Met; (2) V4's measured values (10,980 +-330; 33.6 +-1.0) DIFFER from V3's (11,210 +-330; 34.2 +-1.0), so it is a separate measurement and not a repeated row; (3) Table 2 lists Val/N1, Val/N2, Val/N3, Val/N4 and Val/Nc - the same five positions it lists for Ile, Leu, Met and Gly. The peptide's own name therefore fixes the intended sequence uniquely: AAAVAAAARAAARGGY. Corrected in the TSV with the reason carried in the new `flags` column, same treatment as the Doig 1995 'N-terminus'/'C-terminus' labelling slip. WHY IT MATTERED: uncorrected, V3 and V4 collapse into ONE row of REFERENCE_RUN_LIST.tsv, so V4 would have received no reference run at all and its measurement would have been scored against V3's prediction. The extractor now enforces the invariant that would have caught it at extraction time - every peptide named <X><n> must carry residue X at position n - and it raises if the printed typo is ever not there, so the correction cannot outlive its justification.
1998_petukhov_jmb278.columns_note: A `flags` column was added at cycle 92 to carry the V4 note. It is empty for the other 29 peptides.

1995_doig_protsci4_table1.citation: Doig, A.J. & Baldwin, R.L. (1995). N- and C-capping preferences for all 20 amino acids in alpha-helical peptides. Protein Sci. 4, 1325-1336.
1995_doig_protsci4_table1.source_table: Table 1 - 'Helix contents for peptides with varying N-terminal amino acid'
1995_doig_protsci4_table1.transcription_method: READ FROM THE PAGE RENDERED AT 250-280 dpi, not parsed. The PDF's text layer is an OCR of a scanned print and is corrupted exactly where it matters: -17,100 appears as '-17,1OOc' (letter O for zero), 'Cys-' as 'cys-', 'Trp' as 'TrP', -18,800 as '-18,8We'. Parsing it would have produced plausible-looking wrong numbers. Same method as the Lacroix supplementary Table I at cycle 68 and Scholtz Figure 2 at cycle 64.
1995_doig_protsci4_table1.self_consistency_check: The table prints both -[theta]222 and fraction helix, and footnote b states fraction = -[theta]222/34,100. 43 of 45 populated cells reproduce that to within 0.002; the two exceptions (Asp-, Asp0) differ by 0.002 and 0.004, which is the paper's own rounding. A misread digit in either column would have broken this, so it is a real check on the transcription, not a formality.
1995_doig_protsci4_table1.conditions_quote: 'All measurements were made at 273 K.' / 'The pH 5 buffer contained 1 M NaCl, 5 mM sodium phosphate, 5 mM sodium borate, and 5 mM sodium citrate. The pH 9.55 buffer contained 1 M NaCl, 5 mM sodium phosphate, 5 mM sodium borate, and 5 mM sodium citrate.' (CD measurements) / 'All data are at 273 K in 1 M NaCl.' (Table 1 footnote a)
1995_doig_protsci4_table1.host_quote: 'The peptide sequence is NH2-XAKAAAAKAAAAKAAGY-CONH2. Data are at pH 9.55 (uncharged N-terminus), pH 5 (charged N-terminus)' (Table 1 footnote a)
1995_doig_protsci4_table1.conversion_note: CORRECTED at cycle 87. This is NOT a distinct convention. -34,100 is Scholtz 1991's own -40,000*(1 - 2.5/n) evaluated at the 17-residue host: -40,000*(1-2.5/17) = -34,118, which rounds to the printed -34,100. The same identity holds for the -33,750 of the 16-residue AQ peptides: -40,000*(1-2.5/16) = -33,750 EXACTLY. Padmanabhan 1994's own Methods make it explicit, giving '+640 and -40,000[1 - (2.5/n)] for 0% and 100% helix' in the text while its Table 2 footnote prints the flat -34,100. So this corpus holds TWO theta_H conventions, not five: Scholtz 1991's -40,000(1-2.5/n) (Chakrabartty 1993 and 1994, Doig 1995, Padmanabhan 1994, Huygues-Despointes 1993 - the whole Baldwin lab, internally consistent) and Chen 1974's -39,500(1-2.57/n) (Petukhov 1998, Viguera 1995). The earlier note claimed a third, fourth and fifth and was wrong.
1995_doig_protsci4_table1.flags_note: The table's own footnote letters are carried in the `flags` column: c = from Chakrabartty et al. (1993a), d = from Doig et al. (1994), e = Trp values 'probably highly inaccurate because of Trp extinction coefficient', g = 'inaccurate because of aromatic effect on CD spectrum' (Tyr, Phe), f = corrected value, emitted as a separate `helix_fraction_corrected` row rather than replacing the printed one.
1995_doig_protsci4_table1.why_it_matters: Measures every one of the 20 amino acids at the N-cap position of a single fixed host, at two ionisation states of the alpha-amino group. The reference binary's 14 runs contain SIX residues in total (A G K R S Y), so this covers all fourteen that are otherwise unvalidated - the gap N054@1 names as the likeliest cause of the Munoz 1995 failure. It also bears directly on the unresolved conditional N-cap question behind C6/C7.
1995_doig_protsci4_table1.not_yet_extracted: Table 5 ('Peptide sequences and helix contents used') - 11 further peptides including Qref/Q12/Q7,12,17, KAK, XAK and the CCA/CCQ/CCG/CCZ/CCK free-acid C-cap set, several with free C-termini. Table 4 (pKa values) is described in the table3 entry. Table 3 IS NOW EXTRACTED - the earlier text here still listed it as outstanding.

1995_doig_protsci4_table3.citation: Doig, A.J. & Baldwin, R.L. (1995). N- and C-capping preferences for all 20 amino acids in alpha-helical peptides. Protein Sci. 4, 1325-1336.
1995_doig_protsci4_table3.source_table: Table 3 - 'Helix contents for peptides with varying C-terminal amino acid'
1995_doig_protsci4_table3.transcription_method: READ FROM THE PAGE RENDERED AT 250-280 dpi, not parsed. The PDF's text layer is an OCR of a scanned print and is corrupted exactly where it matters: -17,100 appears as '-17,1OOc' (letter O for zero), 'Cys-' as 'cys-', 'Trp' as 'TrP', -18,800 as '-18,8We'. Parsing it would have produced plausible-looking wrong numbers. Same method as the Lacroix supplementary Table I at cycle 68 and Scholtz Figure 2 at cycle 64.
1995_doig_protsci4_table3.self_consistency_check: 44 of 44 populated cells reproduce footnote b's -[theta]222/34,100 to within 0.002. No exceptions.
1995_doig_protsci4_table3.conditions_quote: 'All data are at 273 K in 1 M NaCI.' (Table 3 footnote a) / Methods, for THIS table's two pH values: 'The pH 1 buffer contained 1 M NaCI, 1 mM sodium phosphate, 1 mM sodium borate, and 1 mM sodium citrate. All measurements were made at 273 K.' / 'The buffer used for pH titrations contained 1 M NaCl, 1 mM sodium phosphate, 1 mM sodium borate, and 1 mM sodium citrate.'
1995_doig_protsci4_table3.host_quote: 'The peptide sequence is Ac-YGAAKAAAAKAAAAKAX-CO2H. Data are at pH 1 (uncharged N-terminus), pH 7 (charged N-terminus)' (Table 3 footnote a)
1995_doig_protsci4_table3.paper_labelling_error:
RESOLVED at cycle 86, after the question's owner objected that a peer-reviewed paper is unlikely to swap N for C uncaught. It is a word-level slip that propagated through the C-cap section, and the authors' own numbers prove it independently of any interpretation.

WHERE THE LABEL IS WRONG: Table 3's four column headers, Table 3's footnote a, TABLE 4's column header, and one sentence of the 'Helix contents of C-cap peptides' Results text - all say 'N-terminus'. Verified at 400-420 dpi, not from the OCR layer.

WHERE IT IS RIGHT: both table titles ('...varying C-terminal amino acid', 'pKa values in C-cap peptides'), and the prose wherever the authors are actually reasoning - 'The pKa's of the C-termini and the C-terminal side chains in the peptides (Table 4) are each around 1 pH unit higher than those of the free amino acids ... caused by the absence of the adjacent NH3+ group ... and the nearby presence of CO groups in the helix and THE NEGATIVE END OF THE HELIX DIPOLE.'

THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE: Table 4's column headed 'pKa, N-terminus' contains 3.12, 3.21, 2.88, 3.14, 3.13, 2.81, 3.50. A peptide alpha-amino group has pKa ~7.5-8; a C-terminal carboxyl has pKa ~3.1-3.5. Those numbers can only be carboxyls. The authors measured C-termini, reasoned about C-termini, and labelled the column 'N-terminus'.

WHY IT SURVIVED REVIEW: the titles, the peptide sequence, the buffers, the pH values, the numbers and every conclusion are correct. Only a recurring noun is wrong, in a section written by adapting the N-cap section. Nothing a reviewer checks - method, chemistry, conclusions - is affected.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS DATASET: none. pH 1 = uncharged C-terminal COOH and pH 7 = charged COO- is the correct assignment and is what the `flags` column records.

This is NOT a distinct convention. -34,100 is Scholtz 1991's own -40,000*(1 - 2.5/n) evaluated at the 17-residue host: -40,000*(1-2.5/17) = -34,118, which rounds to the printed -34,100. The same identity holds for the -33,750 of the 16-residue AQ peptides: -40,000*(1-2.5/16) = -33,750 EXACTLY. Padmanabhan 1994's own Methods make it explicit, giving '+640 and -40,000[1 - (2.5/n)] for 0% and 100% helix' in the text while its Table 2 footnote prints the flat -34,100. So this corpus holds TWO theta_H conventions, not five: Scholtz 1991's -40,000(1-2.5/n) (Chakrabartty 1993 and 1994, Doig 1995, Padmanabhan 1994, Huygues-Despointes 1993 - the whole Baldwin lab, internally consistent) and Chen 1974's -39,500(1-2.57/n) (Petukhov 1998, Viguera 1995). The earlier note claimed a third, fourth and fifth and was wrong.
1995_doig_protsci4_table3.flags_note: CORRECTED at cycle 85. Table 3 uses DIFFERENT footnote letters from Table 1 and the first version of this note assumed they matched. Table 3's are: **c = 'Probably highly inaccurate because of aromatic effect on CD spectrum'**, **d = 'Corrected value (see text)'** (emitted as a separate `helix_fraction_corrected` row), **e = 'From Chakrabartty et al. (1993a)'**. Table 1's, for contrast, are c = from Chakrabartty 1993a, d = from Doig 1994, e = Trp extinction-coefficient inaccuracy, f = corrected value, g = aromatic CD inaccuracy. The letters carried in the data were transcribed from the table and are correct; only this legend was wrong. Sanity check that it is now right: Table 3's 'c' falls on exactly Tyr, Phe and Trp - the three aromatics - and nothing else.
1995_doig_protsci4_table3.values_to_spot_check: CORRECTED at cycle 87 and then VERIFIED CELL BY CELL against the page rendered at 300-420 dpi; all 50 populated cells in both columns reproduce. The earlier note named the wrong pairs. The rows carrying IDENTICAL printed values are, at pH 1 (uncharged C-terminus): Gln/Gly (both -18,300 / 0.537), Amide/Met (both -18,200 / 0.534), Ser/Val (both -15,800 / 0.463). At pH 7 (charged): Ala/Gly (-15,200), His+/Phe (-14,700), Leu/Lys+ (-15,000), Ser/Val (-13,800), Pro/Ile (-13,500). The earlier note listed 'Gln/Met (-18,300 / -18,200 ... close but distinct)', which are the right numbers against the wrong partners, and it missed four of the eight pairs entirely. Every one of them is genuine in the paper - the footnote-b self-consistency check cannot catch a duplicated ROW, which is why they were read off the render.
1995_doig_protsci4_table3.why_it_matters: The C-cap counterpart of Table 1. Together they measure all 20 amino acids at BOTH capping positions on fixed hosts, at two ionisation states each - the single largest addition to residue coverage available from this corpus.
1995_doig_protsci4_table3.spot_check_status: Spot-checked by the question's owner at cycle 85 and reported OK. Marked PROVISIONALLY VERIFIED - a sample was checked, not every cell. The four identical row-pairs noted below were the specific target of that check.
1995_doig_protsci4_table3.related_table_not_extracted: Table 4, 'pKa values in C-cap peptides': terminal pKa 2.81-3.50 for Asp, Cys, His, Glu, Pro, Arg, Lys and side-chain pKa 4.56 (Asp), 9.14 (Cys), 7.68 (His), 4.61 (Glu). Not extracted because it is pKa data rather than helicity, but it is DIRECTLY RELEVANT to this investigation: pyagadir's pKa table is one of the things correction C5 adjusts, and these are measured C-terminal and side-chain pKa values in a helical peptide at 273 K in 1 M NaCl. Worth extracting if the pKa handling is revisited.
1995_doig_protsci4_table3.buffer_correction: CORRECTED at cycle 87. The earlier note said 'buffers as in Table 1', which is wrong. Table 1's two buffers (pH 5 and pH 9.55) are 5 mM in each of phosphate, borate and citrate; Table 3's pH 1 buffer is 1 mM in each, and no pH 7 buffer is described separately - the 1 mM titration buffer is the only candidate. IMMATERIAL for the coded ionic strength, because 1 M NaCl dominates either way (computed I = 1.000 at pH 1 and 1.007 at pH 7 against 1.048 for Table 1 at pH 9.55, all within 5% of the coded 1.0). Recorded because the provenance claim was false, not because a number changes.

1994_chakrabartty_protsci3_table1.citation: Chakrabartty, A., Kortemme, T. & Baldwin, R.L. (1994). Helix propensities of the amino acids measured in alanine-based peptides without helix-stabilizing side-chain interactions. Protein Sci. 3, 843-852.
1994_chakrabartty_protsci3_table1.source_table: Table 1 - 'Sequences and helix contents of peptides'
1994_chakrabartty_protsci3_table1.transcription_method: READ FROM THE PAGE RENDERED AT 200-260 dpi. The PDF's text layer is an OCR of a scanned print and is UNUSABLE for sequences: 12 of its 58 contain characters that are not amino acids - KAJAAK, KA~AAKAyAAK, KA_LAAK, YGGgAAAAg, YCGQ for YGGQ. A parse would have produced plausible-looking wrong peptides, which is worse than no data because a wrong sequence silently yields a wrong prediction.
1994_chakrabartty_protsci3_table1.validation: Every sequence is checked against the 20-letter amino-acid alphabet by the extractor, which raises on any stray character. The 17 N*-GY rows independently reproduce Doig 1995 Table 1's 'c'-flagged uncharged-N-terminus fractions to the last digit (Asn 0.595, Gly 0.525, Ser 0.525, Thr 0.457, Leu 0.449, Ile 0.419, Met 0.402, Pro 0.404, Ala 0.378, Val 0.375, Gln 0.293) on the same host - a cross-paper confirmation of both transcriptions.
1994_chakrabartty_protsci3_table1.residues_present: A C F G I K L M N P Q S T V W Y (16 of 20; no D, E, H, R)
1994_chakrabartty_protsci3_table1.conditions_quote: 'f_helix = [theta]222^obs/(-40,000[1 - 2.5/chain length]). Conditions: 0 C, 1.0 M NaCl, 1 mM each of sodium borate, sodium citrate, and sodium phosphate; pH 7.0 for acetylated peptides and pH 9.55 for unacetylated peptides.' (Table 1 footnote a)
1994_chakrabartty_protsci3_table1.conversion_note: Scholtz 1991's convention. This is NOT a distinct convention. -34,100 is Scholtz 1991's own -40,000*(1 - 2.5/n) evaluated at the 17-residue host: -40,000*(1-2.5/17) = -34,118, which rounds to the printed -34,100. The same identity holds for the -33,750 of the 16-residue AQ peptides: -40,000*(1-2.5/16) = -33,750 EXACTLY. Padmanabhan 1994's own Methods make it explicit, giving '+640 and -40,000[1 - (2.5/n)] for 0% and 100% helix' in the text while its Table 2 footnote prints the flat -34,100. So this corpus holds TWO theta_H conventions, not five: Scholtz 1991's -40,000(1-2.5/n) (Chakrabartty 1993 and 1994, Doig 1995, Padmanabhan 1994, Huygues-Despointes 1993 - the whole Baldwin lab, internally consistent) and Chen 1974's -39,500(1-2.57/n) (Petukhov 1998, Viguera 1995). The earlier note claimed a third, fourth and fifth and was wrong. Only f_helix is printed in this table, so unlike the other datasets the raw ellipticity is NOT recoverable - a real limitation of the table, not of the extraction.
1994_chakrabartty_protsci3_table1.flags_note: b = from Chakrabartty et al. (1993b), c = from Chakrabartty et al. (1993a), d = f_helix corrected for aromatic contributions to theta222, emitted as a separate `helix_fraction_corrected` row (W16, Y16).
1994_chakrabartty_protsci3_table1.overlap_warning: The 17 rows flagged 'c' are the SAME MEASUREMENTS as Doig 1995 Table 1's 'c'-flagged uncharged-N-terminus column, and the 6 flagged 'b' come from Chakrabartty et al. (1993b). They are not independent of those datasets and must not be double-counted if both are ever scored.
1994_chakrabartty_protsci3_table1.why_it_matters: 58 peptides at 16 residues, mostly at INTERIOR helix positions (the YGG-1X, YGG-3X, X-GGY and 2X-GGY series place the test residue in the middle of the chain), which complements Doig's capping-position coverage. It also contains TWO FREE-C-TERMINUS peptides, YG-AC and YG-GC - partially filling a standing data request, since 361 of the 369 points in the scored benchmark are amidated and CT83 (the delivered revision's only empirical constant) is therefore barely tested.

1993_huyghues_protsci2_tables1_2.citation: Huyghues-Despointes, B.M.P., Scholtz, J.M. & Baldwin, R.L. (1993). Effect of a single aspartate on helix stability at different positions in a neutral alanine-based peptide. Protein Sci. 2, 1604-1611.
1993_huyghues_protsci2_tables1_2.source_table: Table 1 (names + sequences) joined to Table 2 ('Dependence of the helix-stabilizing effect of the charge-helix dipole interaction on NaCl concentration')
1993_huyghues_protsci2_tables1_2.transcription_method: READ FROM THE PAGES RENDERED AT 265-300 dpi. The text layer pairs the NAMES and SEQUENCES IN DIFFERENT ORDERS - parsed naively, D7 acquires a sequence with Asp at position 9 - and renders '-NH2' as '-NH,' and 'Ac-' as 'At-'. The rendered table gives the correct pairing.
1993_huyghues_protsci2_tables1_2.validation: Three independent checks, all in the extractor. (1) Every sequence is 16 residues with EXACTLY ONE Asp. (2) For the unstarred series the Asp position equals the number in the peptide's name, for all ten. (3) Converting Table 2's 0.01 M / pH 7.0 column with Scholtz's theta_H (-40,000(1-2.5/16) = -33,750) reproduces the SCORED benchmark's Figure 1 digitisation for all ten shared peptides to within 0.019, systematically 0.004-0.019 low - which is what digitisation error on the figure looks like.
1993_huyghues_protsci2_tables1_2.conditions_quote: 'The helix contents of the AQ and AQ* peptides at NaCl concentrations of 0.01 and 4.8 M at pH 7.0 and pH 2.5 are shown in Table 2.' / Table 2 footnote a: 'Mean residue ellipticity (deg cm2 dmol-1) at 0 C.' / Methods: 'diluting aqueous stock solutions into 10 mM NaCl buffered with 1 mM sodium citrate, 1 mM sodium phosphate, and 1 mM sodium borate (CD buffer)'
1993_huyghues_protsci2_tables1_2.pH_note: The table's acid column is headed 'pH 2.0-2.5'; coded as 2.25 with the range kept in `flags`.
1993_huyghues_protsci2_tables1_2.hosts: Two. The unstarred series (D1..D15) is Ac-AAQAAAAQAAAAQAAY-NH2 with one Ala->Asp substitution. The starred series (D5*..D8*) moves the first two glutamines, giving Ac-AAQAAAAQAAAAQAY-type hosts; it exists to test the Gln-Asp (i,i+4) hydrogen bond. They are DIFFERENT HOSTS and are marked in `flags`.
1993_huyghues_protsci2_tables1_2.why_it_matters: THE IONIC-STRENGTH LEVER THE INVESTIGATION HAS NEVER HAD. Every reference-binary run is at I = 0.05 M and the scored benchmark varies ionic strength essentially not at all - question.md v2(a) has recorded 'no evidence bearing on the temperature lever' since cycle 13 and the same is true of screening. Here the same 14 peptides are measured at 0.01 M AND 4.8 M, at two pH values, giving a 2x2 design on one host. It directly probes the Debye screening and the eq.(12) ionic term, which are currently pinned from a single ionic strength.
1993_huyghues_protsci2_tables1_2.recommendation_for_the_scored_benchmark: The scored `huygues` dataset currently holds values DIGITISED FROM FIGURE 1. Table 2 prints the same measurements as numbers. Replacing the digitised values with the printed ones would remove a 0.004-0.019 digitisation error from ten of the suite's 369 points, and would add the 4.8 M column as new conditions. That changes the scored suite, so it is flagged here rather than done.
1993_huyghues_protsci2_tables1_2.ionic_strength_note: ADDED at cycle 87 (reasoning/evidence/scripts/ionic_strength.py). The coded values are the NaCl concentrations; the CD buffer's own 1 mM each of sodium citrate, sodium phosphate and sodium borate is not in them. At high salt this is immaterial (4.807 vs 4.8; 1.007 vs 1.0). At LOW salt it is not: I = 0.0172 M against the coded 0.010, i.e. 1.7x. Worse for the purpose these datasets were extracted for, the buffer's own charge is pH-dependent - citrate is ~80% trivalent at pH 7 and essentially protonated at pH 2.25 - so the low-salt rows are I = 0.0172 at pH 7 but I = 0.0107 at pH 2.25. The pH 7 vs pH 2.5 comparison that is the whole point of these papers therefore carries a real 1.6x ionic-strength difference which the coding currently records as no difference at all. Not changed unilaterally; this is the sharpest of the ionic-strength flags.

1993_huyghues_protsci2_aspargglurg.citation: Huyghues-Despointes, B.M.P., Klingler, T.M. & Baldwin, R.L. (1993). Helical peptides with three pairs of Asp-Arg and Glu-Arg residues in different orientations and spacings. Protein Sci. 2, 80-85.
1993_huyghues_protsci2_aspargglurg.source_table: Table 1 ('Peptide sequences', repeat notation) joined to Table 2 ('Mean residue ellipticities of Asp-Arg and Glu-Arg peptides')
1993_huyghues_protsci2_aspargglurg.transcription_method: Read from page 2 RENDERED AT 280 dpi; both tables sit side by side and were read together.
1993_huyghues_protsci2_aspargglurg.validation: Four checks in the extractor, each able to fail. (1) Each sequence expanded from its repeat notation must match the length PRINTED in Table 1 (16 or 17). (2) Every sequence must contain exactly three acidic residues and three Arg. (3) The acidic-Arg separation within the repeat unit must equal the i+3 / i+4 in the peptide's own name. (4) Alphabet check against the 20 amino acids.
1993_huyghues_protsci2_aspargglurg.conditions_quote: 'Samples were prepared for CD analysis at 222 nm by diluting the stock solution with a buffer consisting of 1 mM sodium citrate, 1 mM sodium borate, and 1 mM sodium phosphate (CD buffer). ... NaCl dependences were measured by adding incremental volumes of 5 M NaCl in CD buffer' / 'measured at 0 C in 10 mM NaCl, for both the Asp-Arg and ...' / Table 2 footnote b: 'Mean residue ellipticity at 222 nm. Error in -[theta]222 is +-500 (deg cm2 dmol-1).'
1993_huyghues_protsci2_aspargglurg.error_note: The paper's own +-500 deg cm2 dmol-1 is carried in the `error` column on every row.
1993_huyghues_protsci2_aspargglurg.why_it_matters: A SALT-BRIDGE GEOMETRY SERIES CARRYING ACIDIC RESIDUES. Asp and Glu appear in NO reference-binary run - a gap flagged at five successive structural reviews and never closed - and here they are paired with Arg at i,i+3 AND i,i+4, in BOTH orientations (acidic-first and basic-first), at two ionic strengths and two pH values. That is a direct probe of the sidechain-sidechain electrostatics and of tables 4a/4b, which is the question this investigation was opened on. The orientation pairs are the sharpest part: i+4 AB reaches -25,200 at pH 7 where i+4 BA reaches only -14,000 on the same spacing and composition.

1995_viguera_biochem34_table1.citation: Viguera, A.R. & Serrano, L. (1995). Side-chain interactions between sulfur-containing amino acids and phenylalanine in alpha-helices. Biochemistry 34, 8771-8779.
1995_viguera_biochem34_table1.source_table: Table 1 - 'CD Analysis of the Peptides and Determination of the Free Energy of Interaction between the Different Side Chains Being Considered'
1995_viguera_biochem34_table1.transcription_method: Table 1 read from page 5 RENDERED AT 250 dpi; the host sequence read from page 2. NEITHER is recoverable from the text layer - the sequence appears only as spelled-out three-letter names in running prose and a regex over the whole text finds no peptide at all.
1995_viguera_biochem34_table1.host_quote: 'we have designed a template peptide with the sequence Tyr-Gly-Gly-Ser-Ala-Ala-Glu-Ala-X-Ala-Lys-Ala-Y-Ala-Arg-NH2, where X at position 9 and Y at position 13 represent the two positions mutated to Cys, Met, or Phe (Ala in the reference peptides). This peptide has a capping box motif at the N-terminus ... and the C-terminus is blocked' (Results, Peptide Design)
1995_viguera_biochem34_table1.host: YGGSAAEAXAKAYAR, free N-terminus, amidated C-terminus; peptide names are X followed by Y
1995_viguera_biochem34_table1.conditions_quote: CD, Methods: 'Single scans in the range between 180 and 250 nm were obtained at a temperature of 278 K by taking points every 0.2 nm with a 1-s integration time and a 1-nm slit width. Cells with path lengths of 0.01 and 0.5 cm were used for the analysis of peptide concentrations of 500 and 10 microM, respectively.' / Figure 3 legend: 'Conditions: [peptide] = 0.50 mM; 278 K; pH = 3.0 in water.' / Aggregation: 'At pH 7.0 the peptides aggregated. At pH 3.0 no significant changes in the far-UV CD spectra were found in the 10 microM to 0.5 mM range, indicating that the peptides are basically monomeric in water.'
1995_viguera_biochem34_table1.ionic_strength_derivation: DERIVED and weak; unchanged at cycle 87 but now with the counter-argument recorded. 'in water at pH 3.0' with no added salt puts I from the HCl at 1 mM, which is what 0.001 codes. But the PEPTIDE is not neutral here: at pH 3 the free alpha-amino group, Lys11 and Arg15 are protonated and Glu7 is not, giving a net +3, so at the 0.5 mM CD concentration the peptide and its counterions contribute roughly 3 mM more - I ~ 4 mM, four times the coded value - while at 10 microM they contribute nothing. The paper does not say which concentration produced which number, so the ionic strength of this dataset is uncertain by about 4x and is the least well specified in the corpus. Chemistry note for anyone modelling it: at pH 3 the capping-box Glu7 is PROTONATED, so the S4/E7 capping box is not the charged motif it is at pH 7.

quantities.helix_percent_193nm: helical content from the 193 nm ellipticity, +-3
quantities.helix_percent_222nm: helical content by the method of Chen et al. (1974), +-3
quantities.PREDICTION_agadir_orig: AGADIR's prediction WITHOUT the new interaction values - a prediction, never a target
quantities.PREDICTION_agadir_refit: AGADIR after the authors introduced the fitted interaction energies - a prediction
quantities.dG_interaction: free energy the authors FITTED to reproduce their own column 2; derived, not measured

1995_viguera_biochem34_table1.why_it_matters: Same host family as the Lacroix Figure 4 peptides (YGGS...), with a capping box, and it introduces Cys, Met and Phe - three of the fourteen residues absent from every reference-binary run. It is also the only dataset in the corpus at pH 3 and at ~1 mM ionic strength, so it extends both levers at their low ends. The two independent helicity estimates (193 nm and 222 nm) disagree by up to 6 points on the same peptide, which is a useful measure of how much a 'measured helicity' is really worth.
1995_viguera_biochem34_table1.concentration_correction: CORRECTED at cycle 87. The earlier version quoted 'All the peptides (3 mM) were analyzed in water at pH 3.0 and 278 K' as the CD conditions. That sentence is real and verbatim, but it sits under the heading '1H-NMR Spectroscopy' and is the NMR sample concentration. The CD work is at 500 microM and 10 microM (Methods) or 0.50 mM (Figure 3 legend) - six times lower. pH 3.0 and 278 K are unaffected and were right; only the attribution of the concentration was wrong. Concentration is not a stored column, so no coded value changes.

1994_padmanabhan_protsci3_table2.citation: Padmanabhan, S. & Baldwin, R.L. (1994). Tests for helix-stabilizing interactions between various nonpolar side chains in alanine-based peptides. Protein Sci. 3, 1992-1997.
1994_padmanabhan_protsci3_table2.source_table: Table 2 - 'Helix-stabilizing interaction between X and Leu spaced i, i + 4'
1994_padmanabhan_protsci3_table2.transcription_method: Read from page 3 RENDERED AT 280 dpi. The four host sequences are in the table's own footnotes b-e, printed with presentational spaces around the substituted positions (e.g. 'Ac-Y KAAA X KAA L AKAAAAK-NH2'); the spaces are removed.
1994_padmanabhan_protsci3_table2.validation: Three geometric checks in the extractor, each able to fail. For every host: the length must be 17; there must be exactly ONE fixed Leu besides the X site; and the X-to-Leu separation and their N-to-C order must both match what the peptide's own name and the table's Spacing and orientation columns say. All four hosts pass.
1994_padmanabhan_protsci3_table2.conditions_quote: '% Helix measured at 0 C, 1 M NaCl, pH 7.0 (1 mM each of sodium citrate, sodium phosphate, and sodium borate), peptide concentrations of 15-20 uM ... Error in the measurements of % helix was <=3%. The value of -[theta]222 for 100% helix is taken as -34,100 and the value for 0% helix is +640.' (Table 2 footnote a)
1994_padmanabhan_protsci3_table2.conversion_note: CORRECTED at cycle 87. This is NOT a distinct convention. -34,100 is Scholtz 1991's own -40,000*(1 - 2.5/n) evaluated at the 17-residue host: -40,000*(1-2.5/17) = -34,118, which rounds to the printed -34,100. The same identity holds for the -33,750 of the 16-residue AQ peptides: -40,000*(1-2.5/16) = -33,750 EXACTLY. Padmanabhan 1994's own Methods make it explicit, giving '+640 and -40,000[1 - (2.5/n)] for 0% and 100% helix' in the text while its Table 2 footnote prints the flat -34,100. So this corpus holds TWO theta_H conventions, not five: Scholtz 1991's -40,000(1-2.5/n) (Chakrabartty 1993 and 1994, Doig 1995, Padmanabhan 1994, Huygues-Despointes 1993 - the whole Baldwin lab, internally consistent) and Chen 1974's -39,500(1-2.57/n) (Petukhov 1998, Viguera 1995). The earlier note claimed a third, fourth and fifth and was wrong.
1994_padmanabhan_protsci3_table2.table1_not_extracted: DELIBERATE. Table 1's Z positions are Abu (2-aminobutyric acid), Nval (norvaline) and Nle (norleucine) - non-standard residues for which AGADIR has no parameters, so those rows cannot be predicted and would only add unusable sequences.
1994_padmanabhan_protsci3_table2.why_it_matters: A clean i,i+3 versus i,i+4 hydrophobic-pair series on a fixed host, with BOTH N-to-C orientations and four standard residues (Leu, Val, Ile, Phe). It probes tables 4a/4b directly - the non-charged side-chain-side-chain interaction tables - which no dataset in the scored benchmark exercises. The orientation effect is large and the authors say they cannot explain it: 'the helix content is uniformly greater when X is C-terminal to L compared with X being N-terminal to L. We have no explanation for this effect.' That is a published, unexplained asymmetry a model can be tested against.

1993_chakrabartty_biochem32_table1.citation: Chakrabartty, A., Kortemme, T., Padmanabhan, S. & Baldwin, R.L. (1993). Aromatic side-chain contribution to far-ultraviolet circular dichroism of helical peptides and its effect on measurement of helix propensities. Biochemistry 32, 5560-5565.
1993_chakrabartty_biochem32_table1.transcription_method: Read from page 2 RENDERED AT 280 dpi. The sequences survive the text layer here, but the TWO VALUE COLUMNS DO NOT: several rows carry only one number and the text stream gives no indication which column it belongs to. Read naively it lands in column a; the rendered table shows that for `aak`, `fak` and `aa-ak20` it is column b. THREE OF TEN ROWS would have been silently misassigned.
1993_chakrabartty_biochem32_table1.conditions_quote: 'Mean residue ellipticity at 222 nm (deg cm2/dmol). Conditions: 0 C, pH 7, 1.0 M NaCl, 1 mM each of sodium borate, sodium citrate, and sodium phosphate. Peptide concentration was determined by UV absorbance. Values represent the mean of five measurements.' (footnote a) / 'Peptide concentration was determined by ninhydrin assay. Other conditions are the same as in the first column.' (footnote b)
1993_chakrabartty_biochem32_table1.two_columns_note: The two columns are the SAME measurement with the peptide concentration determined two different ways, so their difference is a direct estimate of that systematic error. On the four peptides where both are given it is -400 to +1500 deg cm2 dmol-1 - about 1-5% - which is a useful floor on how precisely any -[theta]222 in this corpus can be known.
1993_chakrabartty_biochem32_table1.why_it_matters: Carries Tyr, Trp AND Phe on one Ala/Lys host, at both the N-terminus and the C-terminus, plus Ala controls. Trp and Phe appear in NO reference-binary run. This is also the paper that established the aromatic CD artefact - a positive induced band at 222 nm from Tyr - which is WHY the Lacroix peptides are written YGGS... with Gly spacers, and why Doig 1995 flags its Tyr, Trp and Phe rows as inaccurate. The yak/aky pair (Tyr at the N- vs C-terminus) and the yaky/yy-ak20 doubles are the direct measurement of that artefact.

1993_scholtz_biochem32_tables1_2.citation: Scholtz, J.M., Qian, H., Robbins, V.H. & Baldwin, R.L. (1993). The energetics of ion-pair and hydrogen-bonding interactions in a helical peptide. Biochemistry 32, 9668-9676.
1993_scholtz_biochem32_tables1_2.source_table: Table I ('Peptide Sequences') joined to Table II ('Fractional Helicities of Peptides')
1993_scholtz_biochem32_tables1_2.transcription_method: BOTH TABLES READ FROM PAGE 3 RENDERED AT 380-420 dpi. The text layer is unusable for either. Table I prints sequences hyphenated per residue and the layer drops the Lys / Glu-Lys / Lys-Glu block's sequence column ENTIRELY - it lists those four series' names with no sequences at all, so a parse would have silently produced a 9-peptide table instead of 19. Table II's layer mangles row labels (E11 -> 'El 1') and interleaves the six value columns.
1993_scholtz_biochem32_tables1_2.validation: Four checks in the extractor, each able to fail, on every peptide. (1) length is the host's 16. (2) alphabet is the 20 amino acids. (3) the host's Gln at 3, 8, 13 and Tyr at 16 survive untouched - no substitution is meant to land on them, and the extractor also refuses any substitution that would replace a non-Ala. (4) NAME CHECK: the substituted residues and positions are exactly what the peptide's own name says, parsed from it - the invariant that caught Petukhov's V4 at cycle 92. All 19 pass.
1993_scholtz_biochem32_tables1_2.host: Ac-AAQAAAAQAAAAQAAY-NH2, 16 residues. THE SAME PEPTIDE as Scholtz 1991 JACS's Ac-(AAQAA)3Y-NH2, the Huyghues-Despointes 1993a unstarred host, and Munoz 1997 Figure 4A's 16-residue point. Every substitution replaces an Ala; the three Gln and the C-terminal Tyr are fixed.
1993_scholtz_biochem32_tables1_2.conditions_quote: Table II footnote a: 'Fractional helicities were determined from the observed ellipticities ([theta]222) at 0 C as described in Experimental Procedures using [theta]_H = -33 750 and [theta]_C = 640 deg cm2 dmol-1. The errors on the fractional helicities are approximately +-0.01.' / Experimental Measurements: 'diluting the stock solution with a buffer consisting of 1 mM sodium citrate, 1 mM sodium borate, and 1 mM sodium phosphate (CD buffer)' / Results: 'concentrations of NaCl (0.01, 1.0, and 2.5 M)'
1993_scholtz_biochem32_tables1_2.ionic_strength_derivation: The coded values are the STATED NaCl concentrations, matching the convention used for the two Huyghues-Despointes datasets. The Baldwin CD buffer's own 1 mM each of citrate, borate and phosphate is not in them: computed (reasoning/evidence/scripts/ionic_strength.py) the true I is 0.0172 at 0.01 M / pH 7 and 0.0107 at 0.01 M / pH 2.5 - so the lowest-salt column is 1.7x low at pH 7 and 1.07x at pH 2.5, while the 1.0 and 2.5 M columns are within 1%. Same flag as the Huyghues datasets and the same reason for not changing it unilaterally: it feeds the scored suite.
1993_scholtz_biochem32_tables1_2.conversion_note: Scholtz 1991's convention, stated here as the evaluated pair rather than the formula: -33,750 IS -40,000*(1-2.5/16) exactly, for this 16-residue host, and +640 is the coil baseline. Only the fractional helicity is printed in Table II, so unlike most of this corpus the raw ellipticity is NOT recoverable - a limitation of the table, not of the extraction. The paper's own error of +-0.01 is carried on every row.
1993_scholtz_biochem32_tables1_2.error_note: The paper's '+-0.01' on the fractional helicities is carried in the `error` column of all 114 rows.
1993_scholtz_biochem32_tables1_2.why_it_matters: THE BEST IONIC-STRENGTH LEVER IN THE CORPUS. 19 peptides on ONE host at THREE NaCl concentrations and TWO pH values - three salt points where Huyghues-Despointes gives two, on a host whose only titratable groups are the substituted residues themselves, so the salt axis is not confounded. It is simultaneously a Glu/Lys ion-pair series at i,i+1 (E5K6), i,i+2 (E5K7), i,i+3 (E6K9) and i,i+4 (E6K10) in the Glu-first orientation and i,i+3 (K6E9) / i,i+4 (K6E10) in the Lys-first one, with the single-substitution Glu and Lys series as their own controls - a direct probe of tables 4a/4b with the controls built in. The AQ row is also what confirmed N050's normalisation hypothesis at cycle 93.
1993_scholtz_biochem32_tables1_2.cross_reference: The AQ host row (0.49 / 0.52 / 0.48) is the peptide at Munoz 1997 Figure 4A's 16-residue point. See pyagadir/data/validation/munoz_1997_figure_4_data.json _provenance.per_panel.figure4A and reasoning/nodes/N050.md@4.
1993_scholtz_biochem32_tables1_2.related_tables_not_extracted: Tables III, IV and V ('Side-Chain Interactions' at 10 mM, 1.0 M and 2.5 M NaCl) are FITTED interaction free energies derived from Table II, not measurements, and are deliberately not stored - the same treatment the Viguera 1995 dG_interaction column gets.
